clue.text: In middle distance, I entered university environment

indicators.note: the letter I goes inside the distance word, entering it

parts.note: the mile is the classic middle-distance race on the track

explanation.surface: A student describes running middle distance after arriving at university.
explanation.definitionFit: A milieu is the social setting or surroundings in which someone lives.

clue.text: Dispute having a test about nothing

indicators.note: the test's letters go round the zero, sitting about it

parts.note: the MOT is the annual British roadworthiness test for vehicles
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone argues over taking an exam on which nothing depends.
explanation.walkthrough: The MOT is Britain's yearly compulsory vehicle safety check.
explanation.definitionFit: To moot a point is to raise it for debate, to argue it out.

clue.text: Butter up some wild (initially tame) animal

indicators.note: in a down clue the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a ram butts with its head, so it is a butter

indicators.note: wild signals that the letters of 'some' run riot into a new order
initially means take just the opening letter of 'tame'

explanation.surface: Flatter a wild animal, which is tame at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butter up' looks like flattery; 'Butter' is in fact a ram, the animal that butts, and 'up' is the reversal in a down clue, while 'wild' shuffles the four letters of 'some'.
explanation.definitionFit: A marmoset is a small South American monkey, an example of an animal.

clue.text: They try to breed chess champions

definitions.meaning: people who pair animals for breeding, those who mate them
chess winners deliver checkmate, so they are those who mate

explanation.surface: Ambitious parents try to raise a family of chess prodigies.
explanation.definitionFit: Breeders pair animals off and chess winners checkmate the opposing king: both are, literally, those who mate.

clue.text: Work in a plant erected in China

indicators.note: the letters go inside the friend word, in it

parts.note: china is rhyming slang for mate, from china plate

indicators.note: in a down clue, erected means the word is put up, so read backwards

parts.note: a lupin is a garden flowering plant

explanation.surface: A man working with a plant that has been put up in China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China plate' is Cockney rhyming slang for mate (friend). 'erected' turns the plant upward in this down clue, and 'in' places A and the turned plant inside the friend.
explanation.definitionFit: To manipulate something is to work it skilfully with the hands.

clue.text: Prate as a result of this Wednesday's sol instruction for STRAPPED hardware

annotationWithheld.clue: Prate as a result of this Wednesday's sol instruction for STRAPPED hardware

clue.text: Power base wants volunteers back in outfit

indicators.note: the other letters go inside the outfit word

parts.note: a kit is a set of clothes, an outfit
base in the sense of low, mean

indicators.note: back means the reserve's letters are read in reverse

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: A powerful base needs volunteers back in uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: The TA (Territorial Army) is the British volunteer reserve force; 'back' turns it to AT.
explanation.definitionFit: A kilowatt is a thousand watts, a unit measuring electrical power.

clue.text: Unofficially handle weight above a setter

indicators.note: in a down clue, above places the weight first, over the rest

parts.note: a ton is a heavy unit of weight
the setter refers to themselves as me

explanation.surface: A heavy weight above the puzzle-maker, managed informally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'handle' is slang for a name; a to-name is a Scots word for a byname or nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: Handle is slang for a person's name, and a to-name is an added nickname used informally.

clue.text: Slow ace one serves in trouble

indicators.note: the pieces go inside the trouble word

parts.note: ado means fuss or trouble
A stands for ace in cards
a GI is an American soldier, one who serves

explanation.surface: A tennis player's slow ace serve lands them in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is tennis, but 'one serves' is a GI, a US serviceman.
explanation.definitionFit: Adagio is the musical direction for a slow tempo.

clue.text: Garment 7 cut out slightly off-centre

indicators.note: four letters are removed from just right of the middle of the referenced word

parts.note: refers to the answer at 7 across, a unit of power

explanation.surface: A garment is trimmed a little off-centre.
explanation.walkthrough: From KILOWATT (7 across), removing OWAT, the letters four to seven, just past the centre, leaves KILT.
explanation.definitionFit: A kilt is the pleated knee-length skirt of Scottish Highland dress, a garment.

clue.text: One vomited — terrible — or capital!

indicators.note: terrible suggests the letters of the phrase are thrown into chaos

explanation.surface: Someone was terribly sick, or else it was a great time.
explanation.definitionFit: Montevideo is the capital city of Uruguay.

clue.text: Muskrats endlessly soiled shirts in 25?

indicators.note: soiled suggests a messing up of the letters into a new order
endlessly means the first and last letters of 'Muskrats' are dropped

explanation.surface: Muskrats have dirtied the shirts in some Indian state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' leaves USKRAT and 'soiled' rearranges it. 25 across is Kerala, an Indian state.
explanation.definitionFit: Kurtas are loose collarless tunics worn in South Asia, including the Indian state at 25.

clue.text: Canine itch sorted by expert

indicators.note: sorted means the letters are put into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A dog's itch is dealt with by a specialist.
explanation.definitionFit: A technician is a skilled practitioner of a craft, an expert in its technique.

clue.text: Little man breaking low buzzer

indicators.note: the little man splits the cow's sound open, breaking into it

parts.note: to low is to moo like a cow
a squit is slang for an insignificant little person

explanation.surface: A small man breaking down with a low buzzing noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'low' is the cow's call, not 'not high'; 'squit' is British slang for a small, unimportant person.
explanation.definitionFit: The mosquito is an insect named for its whine, a buzzer.

clue.text: Former convict's leader that's accepting time in stir

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter
the abbreviation takes in the time letter, accepting it

parts.note: that is is abbreviated ie

explanation.surface: An ex-con's leader takes some time in jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stir' looks like slang for prison, but it is the definition as a verb, to rouse.
explanation.definitionFit: To stir someone up is to rouse or agitate them.

clue.text: New general bombed part of Germany

indicators.note: bombed signals the letters are blown apart and rearranged

explanation.surface: A new general bombed a region of Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: Erlangen is a university city in Bavaria, a place in Germany.

clue.text: Came upon evenly prepared pitch?

indicators.note: prepared signals letters made ready in a new order
evenly means take the second and fourth letters of 'upon'

explanation.surface: Someone found a well-prepared pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evenly' takes PN from 'upon'; 'prepared' rearranges CAME with them.
explanation.definitionFit: To encamp is to pitch a tent and set up camp; the question mark marks the verb sense.

clue.text: A 17 A number of people accepting, say, denial

indicators.note: the people word takes in the example letters

parts.note: a nation is a large body of people
say means for example, eg

explanation.surface: A country embracing the idea of a refusal.
explanation.walkthrough: The leading 'A 17' as held is stray OCR text before the clue proper.
explanation.definitionFit: Negation is the act of denying or contradicting something.

clue.text: Expel shoplifter, ultimately entering store

indicators.note: the final letter goes into the store word

parts.note: a depot is a storehouse

indicators.note: ultimately means take the final letter of 'shoplifter'

explanation.surface: Throw out a shoplifter who finally came into the shop.
explanation.definitionFit: To deport someone is to expel them from a country.

clue.text: Broadcasts linked OK in a rush

indicators.note: to broadcast is to scatter widely, so the letters are scattered anew

explanation.surface: Radio broadcasts were linked at speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a rush' is the gold rush to Canada's Yukon in the 1890s.
explanation.definitionFit: The Klondike gold rush drew prospectors to the Yukon in 1896-99.

clue.text: Man touring poor African city

indicators.note: the name goes round the other word, touring it

parts.note: Ian is a man's name
bad means poor in quality

explanation.surface: A man touring a poor city in Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibadan is a large city in south-western Nigeria.

clue.text: Man races in run for a quarter?

indicators.note: the pieces go inside the run word

parts.note: go means run, as in operating
he refers to a man
the TT races are the Tourist Trophy motorcycle races on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A man races in a run to cover a quarter-mile.
explanation.walkthrough: The TT (Tourist Trophy) is a famous motorcycle race on the Isle of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghetto is a district of a city, a quarter set apart for one group.

clue.text: A heartless poet's verse

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letters of the poet's name are taken out

parts.note: Tennyson is the Victorian poet

explanation.surface: A poet who lacks heart writes verse.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenson is a troubadour poem written as a debate between poets.

clue.text: A baker's beginning to cut excellent loaf

indicators.note: the pieces cut into the excellent word

parts.note: a knockout is something stunning or excellent

indicators.note: beginning means take the first letter of 'baker's'

explanation.surface: A baker begins to slice an excellent loaf of bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loaf' looks like bread, but it is the verb, to idle about.
explanation.definitionFit: To knock about is to idle around aimlessly, to loaf.

clue.text: Flatten Geordie back inside bingo

indicators.note: the reversed letters go inside the knockout

parts.note: KO is a knockout, which flattens an opponent

indicators.note: back means the region letters are reversed

parts.note: a Geordie is from Newcastle, in the North-East of England, NE

explanation.surface: Knock down a Geordie back inside the bingo hall.
explanation.walkthrough: A Geordie is a native of Newcastle in North-East England.
explanation.definitionFit: Keno is a lottery-style game of chance much like bingo.

clue.text: Fire left smothered by family

indicators.note: the letter is covered over by the family word

parts.note: kin means family

explanation.surface: A fire on the left is smothered by the family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fire' is the verb, to bake pottery.
explanation.definitionFit: To kiln pottery is to bake it, as a potter fires ware.

clue.text: Some agents-general are kept back in a state

indicators.note: back means the part is read in reverse
some means only part of the run of words is used

explanation.surface: Some agents-general are held back in a state.
explanation.definitionFit: Kerala is a state on the south-west coast of India.

clue.text: In addition, sign into party — cheers

parts.note: too means in addition

indicators.note: the sign goes into the party word

parts.note: a do is a party
Leo is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A guest signs into a party and toasts the company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cheers' is the British informal goodbye, not a toast.
explanation.definitionFit: Toodle-oo is a jaunty British farewell, like the informal parting 'cheers'.
